report:
Reviewed the complete review_visibility claim after adding missing source association and a focused capture regression. Both implementation entries and both associated tests are ordinary; there are no TODO/N/A deferrals.
Requirements: inline source, annotations, explicit configuration, and expected observations remain inside the annotated function; review captures the complete macro invocation without its implementation; independent harness review and substantive visible assertions remain necessary; ERROR/WARN and compiler-condition edits require semantic justification rather than blessing alone.
Implementation: compile/mod.rs compile_test! forwards call-site source and expectation expressions into CompileTest, whose run validates preparation before asserting expectations. The macro carries its own invocation anchor and the runner has independent behavioral tests. sage-meta/src/review.rs inventory copies the entire indexed function span into a Test fragment, without macro expansion or adding macro-definition files. Exact fragment comparison in input_errors invalidates the review for any changed invocation text. Its prompt requires evaluating complete claims and actual assertions; the captured contributing instructions explicitly require semantic investigation of marker and compiler-condition changes. That last obligation is a human review rule, not a claim that the executable can prove a semantic rationale.
Tests: blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates contains its complete disposable fixture, source, //# ty selection, expectations, cargo options and assertions in the annotated body. It checks that an unexpected rustc warning blocks updating and preserves bytes, stale observations fail without updating, blessing inserts the actual literal/u16 observation at the call site while preserving source and diagnostics, and the rerun succeeds without writes. The new inline_test_capture_preserves_intent_and_excludes_macro_implementation uses a source-level test fixture with explicit edition, ERROR/WARN qualifiers and an expectation; it asserts exact equality of the captured function, absence of the macro definition in all fragments, continued validity after only a macro-definition change, and invalidity after each severity or compiler-qualifier change. Its Fixture helper constructs an isolated valid source/spec inventory; the meaningful capture and freshness assertions stay in the test body. These assertions would detect truncating macro arguments, capturing expanded/definition text, or ignoring changed marker intent. This is a source capture test, not an assertion that its illustrative diagnostic strings are valid compiler results.
Executed cargo fmt and cargo test -p sage-meta --test review inline_test_capture_preserves_intent_and_excludes_macro_implementation: one test passed. The callsite integration test was inspected but not executed by this reviewer. Build and independent quality checks are coordinated separately. All remaining assessment is source inspection; no runtime compiler correctness beyond the associated test contracts is claimed.
